title: Thanksgiving Fire Safety Tips for King George Residents - NewsBreak
text:
2 hours ago Thanksgiving is a major holiday in King George. Many people use this time to relax with family and friends. However, it is also the leading day for home cooking fires, according to the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA). The risk of fire increases during the holiday, especially with the use of deep-frying methods for turkeys.
Turkey fryers are a common source of Thanksgiving-related fires. These devices can tip over, spill hot oil, or overheat. Using a partially frozen turkey or too much oil can cause spillovers and fires. The sides and handles of fryers can also become very hot and cause burns.
To reduce these risks, use turkey fryers outdoors and away from buildings or flammable materials. Place the fryer on a stable, non-flammable surface. Do not leave the fryer unattended. Keep children and pets away. Make sure the turkey is fully thawed before frying. The National Turkey Federation recommends thawing turkeys in the refrigerator for 24 hours per five pounds.
General kitchen safety is also important. Do not leave cooking unattended. Keep flammable items away from open flames. Have pan lids and a fire extinguisher nearby. Check that smoke alarms and carbon monoxide detectors are working.
By following these safety tips, King George residents can help prevent fires during Thanksgiving. In case of a fire, call 911 right away. Do not use water to put out a grease fire. Stay alert and celebrate the holiday safely.
